title: Finite algebra restriction preserves and reflects relative degreewise pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $R,A,B$ be commutative rings and let $R\to A\to B$ be compatible ring maps. Assume $A$ and $B$ are finitely generated $R$-algebras and $B$ is finitely generated as an $A$-module. Let $m\in\mathbf Z$ and $M\in D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $M$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$ if and only if $\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}M\in D(A)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$ [def-sfb-ring-relative-m-pseudocoherent]. Restriction of scalars is termwise, with the same groups and differentials and with $a$ acting through its image in $B$. The relative predicates on the two sides use the given $R$-algebra structures on $B$ and $A$, respectively. No Noetherian, finite-presentation, flatness or cohomological boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: If $R=0$, unitality forces $A=B=0$, and every unital module is zero since $x=1x=0x=0$. Thus every representing complex is zero; the polynomial presentation with no variables and the zero finite free approximation witness both relative predicates for every $m$. Hence assume $R\ne0$. Choose a finite generating set of $A$ over $R$, giving $\alpha:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$. Choose $y_1,\ldots,y_s\in B$ generating $B$ as an $A$-module. They also generate it as an $A$-algebra: every element is already an $A$-linear combination of them. Evaluation therefore gives a surjection $\gamma:T=P[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]\twoheadrightarrow B$, sending $Y_j$ to $y_j$. This is a finite polynomial presentation over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0673, lemma-finite-extension-pseudo-coherent, first two sentences; zero-ring case made explicit.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], each $y_j$ satisfies a monic equation over $A$. Lift its finitely many lower coefficients through $\alpha$, keeping leading coefficient $1$, to obtain $f_j(Z)\in P[Z]$ with $f_j(y_j)=0$ in $B$. We may take its degree $d_j\geq1$: if the equation is the constant $1$, replace it by $Z$ times that equation before lifting. Put $C=T/(f_1(Y_1),\ldots,f_s(Y_s))$. Here $(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ means all finite sums of ring multiples, and the quotient identifies elements whose difference is in this ideal. The evaluation $\gamma$ factors through $C\to B$, since it kills every generator of the ideal. The composite $P\to C\to B$ is the given $P\to A\to B$ on coefficients and generators.

source.place: Tag 0673, lemma-finite-extension-pseudo-coherent, monic polynomials and commutative diagram.

proof.text: For $0\leq j\leq s$ put $T_j=T/(f_1(Y_1),\ldots,f_j(Y_j))$, so $T_0=T$ and $T_s=C$. The polynomial universal property identifies $T_{j-1}$ with $E_j[Y_j]$, where $E_j=(P[Y_1,\ldots,Y_{j-1}]/(f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1}))[Y_{j+1},\ldots,Y_s]$: the maps fixing all variables and coefficients are inverse. The image of $f_j$ is monic of positive degree in $Y_j$. Multiplication by it is injective, since a nonzero polynomial with top coefficient $c\ne0$ has product with top coefficient $c$ in degree $d_j$ higher. Its cokernel is $T_j$ by definition. Hence $[T_{j-1}\xrightarrow{f_j(Y_j)}T_{j-1}]$, in degrees $-1,0$ and augmented by the quotient, is a bounded finite free resolution of $T_j[0]$. Thus $T_j[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $T_{j-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0673, verification of the top right vertical map against Tag 064Z, expanded one monic equation at a time.

proof.text: Put $D_j=P[Y_1,\ldots,Y_j]/(f_1,\ldots,f_j)$, including $D_0=P$ and $D_s=C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] to $D_j=D_{j-1}[Y_j]/(f_j(Y_j))$. It gives the basis $1,Y_j,\ldots,Y_j^{d_j-1}$ over $D_{j-1}$. Induction gives a $P$-basis of $D_j$ consisting of the products $Y_1^{e_1}\cdots Y_j^{e_j}$ with $0\leq e_i<d_i$: expand a vector in the new power basis and then expand each coefficient in the previous basis; uniqueness at these two stages proves independence. The induction starts with the basis $1$ of the nonzero ring $P$, and the nonempty basis at each stage also shows $D_j\ne0$. Thus $C$ is finite free over $P$. Its degree-zero complex is itself a bounded finite free model, so $C[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $P$. The empty list gives $C=P$.

source.place: Tag 0673, verification of the top horizontal map against Tag 064Z: finite freeness over the polynomial base.

proof.text: Regard $M$ as a $C$-complex through $C\to B$. Apply [lem-sfb-m-pseudocoherent-algebra-scalar-restriction] first to each $T_{j-1}\to T_j$, whose algebra is pseudo-coherent by step 3, and then to $P\to C$, whose algebra is pseudo-coherent by step 4. This gives $$\gamma_*M\text{ is }m\text{-pseudo-coherent over }T\ \Longleftrightarrow\ M|_C\text{ is }m\text{-pseudo-coherent over }C\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (P\to B)_*M\text{ is }m\text{-pseudo-coherent over }P.$$ All restrictions have the same groups and differentials, and the scalar actions agree because the ring maps compose as in step 2. For $s=0$ the first equivalence is the identity. No tensor product or flatness of $A\to B$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0673, final paragraph: two applications of the fixed-m equivalence in Tag 064Z; the quotient application is iterated.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-ring-relative-m-pseudocoherent], relative $m$-pseudo-coherence is the existence of a polynomial presentation with the indicated absolute predicate, using ordinary-module derived restriction induced termwise. The revised definition explicitly supplies this functor; its underlying additive groups and differentials are unchanged. By [lem-sfb-polynomial-presentation-m-pseudocoherence-invariance], existence is equivalent to the predicate on any chosen presentation: compare a witnessing presentation with the chosen one for the forward implication, and use the chosen one as witness for the reverse. Apply this to $A$ with presentation $\alpha$ and to $B$ with presentation $\gamma$. The two resulting absolute predicates are exactly the rightmost and leftmost predicates in step 5, since restriction along $P\to A\to B$ agrees termwise with the composite. Step 5 therefore proves the required equivalence for the given integer $m$.

source.place: Tags 065H and 065I, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent and definition-relatively-pseudo-coherent; conclusion of Tag 0673.
